label: 978-r3
round: candidate-55 round 3 (the owner's exception of 2026-11-10 beyond two reworks), patch 0793
verdict: ready for the testbed; the gate's difference is not #978's
verdict_basis: Cause: #978 (round 2 or 3) does not change how a text-only request is handled. Statically, no line of its engine, scheduler or frontend code is reached by a request without multimodal items beyond an empty-list or empty-dict check, and it changes no KV cache manager, request or worker code. Dynamically, the gate's requests replayed through the real frontend and a real EngineCore/AsyncScheduler/KVCacheManager over DS4.1's KV cache groups give candidate-54's requests byte for byte and its schedule step for step (3,083 steps, every block id, every prefix-cache hit), on round 2 and on round 3, twice each.

The premise that 'again' re-runs prompts on cached blocks does not hold: every 'again' request carries a fresh cache_salt, and the gate's short prompts render to 14-22 tokens, below one 256-token scheduler block, so no request of the gate hits the prefix cache (the 'cached' pairs included). The replay shows 0 cached tokens in every gate scenario.

The gate compares a server with itself: in round 2's boot the reference digests (18d61961, d6568649, text 0a2dacdd, 12fd8257) were candidate-54's, and c8, staggered, mixed, cached and mixed15 were identical. A deterministic change to a text request's path would show in those. What differed was one request of the last scenario, a different prompt in each run (2 with logprobs, 4 without), late in its 192 tokens: a run-to-run difference.

The same kind of difference is on main without #978: candidate-51's gate at tp4-ring (receipts/tp4-ring/determinism/candidate-51-tp4/greedy-candidate-51.jsonl), 'again' prompt 7 from character 112; it was recorded as 'the gate is identical'. Across the 43 recorded 'again' runs on main, 3 have a difference: that one and round 2's two.

Fix (round 3): the two places where round 2 still touched every request are now gated on the request's multimodal items: the engine's request handler adds a request without items with candidate-54's statement and nothing around it, and AsyncLLM._add_request sends it with candidate-54's statement. Both guards read the items with getattr, so request stand-ins without mm_features also take the earlier statements: round 2's _add_request read request.mm_features on every request, and candidate-54's async admission test (test_admission_control.py::test_concurrent_single_request_admission_respects_limit, collected but never run in the release environment, which has no async plugin) fails on round 2's tree when run with asyncio.run and passes on candidate-54 and round 3. Every other line is round 2's. The new test file pins text-request scheduling on prefix-cache re-runs to candidate-54's recorded schedule (passes on candidate-54, round 2 and round 3) and the handler and frontend paths for requests without items (2 of its tests fail on round 2's tree, all pass on candidate-54 and round 3).

Kept: round 2's serving-path gain. Its bench (the mark), ABBA against candidate-54, two boots each, on the final tree: all 12 image cells faster beyond the interval, turn 2+ 4.25x-9.59x, turn 1 2.8%-15.4% faster; prompt token ids and mm hashes equal candidate-54's. Text-only requests, ABBA twice (four boots each): every cell within the interval. With the recipe's frontend environment (supplementary, as round 2's): turn 2+ 4.6x-11.9x and turn 1 faster in 5 of 6 workloads in both sessions; 1920x1080 PNG turn 1 is bimodal by boot exactly as round 2 found it (round 2: 80.9/79.7 against 72.0/70.2 ms, the processor's work on Cortex-A725 cores): on the final tree 3 of 6 boots at 78-80 ms and 3 at 61-64 ms against 69-75 ms, so slower beyond the interval in the 2-boot session and within it in the 4-boot one. Round 3 changes no image path. Also kept: the closed risks, #972's guarantees and round 1's fixes (round 2's tests all pass on round 3: the gate files 68, #978's set 60 on two boots, the directories and the scheduler and multimodal set with candidate-54's failures only).

cause.question: Do round 2's scheduler, engine-core or frontend changes reach text-only requests that re-run on cached blocks (a changed prefix-cache hit length, chunk boundary, computed-token count or scheduling order)?
cause.answer: No. Not in round 2 and not in round 3. The exact mechanism of the one-request 'again' difference at tp4-ring is not established here (one GB10 cannot run the TP4 model); it lies below the scheduler and frontend, which #978 does not touch for text, and it occurs without #978.
cause.what_again_does: token_determinism_text.py (experiments/2026-10-12-r6g): after reference (each prompt alone, fresh salt), c8, staggered, mixed, mixed15 (with --wide) and cached (each prompt twice with one salt, the second compared), 'again' runs the eight prompts one at a time once more, each with a fresh uuid4 cache_salt, and compares them with the reference.
why_no_prefix_cache_hit: cache_salt enters the first block hash (kv_cache_utils.generate_block_hash_extra_keys: [request.cache_salt] for start_token_idx 0), so a fresh salt can match nothing.

DS4.1's KV cache has 18 groups (40 SlidingWindowMLASpec layers of block 128, 8 MLAAttentionSpec of block 256, 3 CircularBufferSpec of 32; read from the worker's own get_kv_cache_spec): the scheduler block is 256 tokens and a hit needs whole blocks of the prompt short of its last token. The gate's prompts render (DS4.1 tokenizer and template, thinking off) to 18, 19, 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 17 tokens (and 14-22 for the seven more), so not even 'cached' hits anything. The long prompt (14,820 tokens) always has a fresh salt.

The replay's prefill stats: num_cached_tokens 0 for every request of every gate scenario; only the re-run beyond the gate with the reference salts gives a hit (the long prompt: 14,592 of 14,820 tokens).
cause.within_server_comparison: Round 2's boot produced candidate-54's reference digests and identical c8, staggered, mixed, cached and mixed15; a deterministic difference in a text request's path would act on the reference and every scenario alike. Only a state- or timing-dependent effect can make the last scenario alone differ, and #978 adds no state that a text request reads or writes (its frontend marks and retry map and the scheduler's miss record stay empty without multimodal requests).
cause.precedent: candidate-51 (candidate-50 without #1009 plus #961, #963, #987's WO-B part and #1001; no #978) at tp4-ring: greedy run, 'again' prompt 7 differs from character 112 (raw/gate-history.json).
leads_not_verified: Physical KV blocks are reused across requests: in the replay, the second reference request's 18 first blocks (32, 18, 31, 17, ...) are all blocks the first one freed, out of 49,483, so every scenario runs on blocks with earlier requests' contents, and which blocks a request gets depends on when the previous request's blocks are freed.

With async scheduling and late admission (VLLM_LATE_ADMISSION_LAYER=30), when a request is first scheduled and when the previous one's blocks are freed depend on timing in the served engine; the replay fixes arrivals by step and so cannot show it.

A difference late in a lone request (output tokens 176, 189; character 641; character 112 on candidate-51) on a different prompt each time fits a rare numeric effect of that placement or timing in the worker's kernels or collectives, not a scheduling or prefix-cache change. Measuring the rate needs repeated gates on a build without #978 (candidate-54 or candidate-55 without #978); the round-3 spec boots the candidate twice.

vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py, AsyncLLM._add_request: 'if getattr(request, "mm_features", None) and self._mm_prefix_fastpath:' the fast path's preparation and its send with the unmark-on-failure handling; else candidate-54's 'await self.engine_core.add_request_async(request)'. Round 2 read request.mm_features on every request and wrapped every send.

static_argument.claim: A text-only request (no multimodal items: EngineCoreRequest.mm_features None, Request.mm_features []) executes candidate-54's statements in the frontend, the engine core and the scheduler; the only additions it passes are the guards listed, each false for it, and none reads or writes state.

frontend.rendering: vllm/renderers/base.py _process_tokens(_async): 'if multi_modal_data := prompt.get("multi_modal_data")' else tokens_input(...): the processor (processor.py, image.py, inputs.py, hasher.py) never runs for a text prompt; renderers/base.py's changes are in __init__ (the processor's flag, the header cache switch), clear_mm_cache and _clear_processor_cache only.
frontend.AsyncLLM._add_request: 'if getattr(request, "mm_features", None) and self._mm_prefix_fastpath:' false -> else branch: 'await self.engine_core.add_request_async(request)' (candidate-54's statement).
frontend.output handler: 'if pending_mm_retries:' per output chunk and before the stop-string abort: the map is filled only by _prepare_mm_features_for_prefix_cache (fast path, items), so it is empty for a text-only server and false for a text request.
frontend.abort: 'if self._mm_prefix_fastpath and self._pending_mm_retries:' false without fast-path items.
frontend.utilities: reset_mm_cache, reset_prefix_cache, reset_encoder_cache and sleep clear the (empty) marks; shutdown cancels the (empty) retry task set: not request paths.
frontend.startup: The renderer's background MM warmup (dummy images, API server only) takes the fast path's processor branch: a helper thread (vllm-mm-hash) hashes beside the HF processor and the dummy's metadata is cleared at the warmup's end (clear_mm_cache). Round 2 the same; no engine or request effect.

engine_core.EngineCoreProc._handle_client_request AD: 'if not getattr(req, "mm_features", None): self.add_request(req, request_wave); return' -> candidate-54's statement.
engine_core.EngineCore.add_request: 'if getattr(request, "mm_features", None) and self.mm_receiver_cache is None:' false: _verify_or_resolve_stripped_mm_features (the only new caller of KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks, which can set request.use_boundary_checkpoints and boundary_checkpoint) is not called; then candidate-54's scheduler.add_request.

scheduler._lacks_mm_data, class attribute, __init_: a helper, 'stripped_mm_misses: ... = None' and 'self.stripped_mm_misses = {}': no request path.
scheduler._try_schedule_encoder_inputs: the schedule-time miss block is inside the per-item loop of a function that returns at once 'if num_new_tokens == 0 or not request.has_encoder_inputs' and whose callers (waiting and running loops) call it only 'if request.has_encoder_inputs'.
scheduler.update_from_output: 'if self.stripped_mm_misses:' (once per step, not per request) is filled only by that block, so it is empty in a text-only engine.
scheduler.untouched: kv_cache_manager.py, kv_cache_coordinator, block_pool, request.py, async_scheduler.py, the worker: not in the patch.

dynamic_evidence.frontend_part: A real AsyncLLM from the served DS4.1 checkpoint with the recipe's flags (--enable-prefix-caching, --mm-processor-cache-gb 0, --limit-mm-per-prompt {image:67}, block size 256, chunked prefill, max-num-seqs 16, max-num-batched-tokens 16384, long-prefill threshold 16288, async scheduling, retention interval 8192, generation-config vllm, the DSpark speculative config), the real OnlineRenderer rendering each gate request as the server does (chat template, thinking off, cache_salt, logprobs, temperature 0, ignore_eos), AsyncLLM.generate; the engine-core client an in-process fake that msgpack-encodes each EngineCoreRequest. Round 2 and 3 run with the fast path on (mm_prefix_fastpath true), candidate-54 without it.
dynamic_evidence.engine_part: A real EngineCore (its __init__) with a stand-in executor that reports DS4.1's KV cache specs (exp/ds41_kv_specs.py: the model built on the meta device, engram table on disk, the worker's own get_kv_cache_spec) and the recipe's 11,274,289,152 KV bytes: the real AsyncScheduler (sink rejection on, as DS4.1's default; 5 speculative tokens; batch queue 2; late admission on) and KVCacheManager over 18 groups and 49,483 blocks. Each request is decoded from the frontend's frames, preprocessed (preprocess_add_request, the block hasher) and enters through EngineCoreProc._handle_client_request (ADD); the loop is step_with_batch_queue. The stand-in model follows the V2 runner's sink-rejection contract (as tests/v1/core/test_sink_draft_zero.py's scripted worker): tokens and accepted drafts are hashes of the request's own history.
dynamic_evidence.workload: The gate in its order and concurrency, in engine steps: reference (alone), the long prompt alone, c8 (together), staggered (8 steps apart), mixed (the long prompt 24 steps later), the seven more alone, mixed15, cached (pairs with one salt), again (alone, fresh salts), then again_salted (the eight and the long prompt with their reference salts: a prefix-cache re-run). 90 requests, 3,083 steps.
dynamic_evidence.recorded: Every step's SchedulerOutput: scheduled tokens and drafts per request, computed tokens and block ids of new requests, new block ids, computed tokens and resumption of running ones, preemptions, finishes, common-prefix blocks, encoder inputs; per request its prefill stats (prompt, computed, cached tokens) and outputs; the frontend's encoded requests (id and arrival time fixed).
dynamic_evidence.result: Byte-identical on all six runs (candidate-54, round 2, round 3, twice each, order none r2 r3 r3 r2 none): frontend requests sha256 ea07da74..., schedule trace 0aca7a2d..., outputs a1e90195...
dynamic_evidence.limits: Arrivals are fixed by step, so the replay cannot show timing effects of the served engine; the stand-in replaces the worker, so worker numerics are not exercised; the drafter's own KV groups are not in the specs (the meta build has the target's layers only). It shows that #978 changes neither what a text request carries into the engine nor any scheduler or KV cache manager decision about it, including on prefix-cache re-runs.

tests.test_text_request_enters_the_engine_as_b: a text request added through EngineCoreProc._handle_client_request is in the scheduler with no prefix lookup before the scheduler's own (KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks first called by schedule()), and an error raised while adding a request without items surfaces unchanged (no multimodal-miss handling around it).
tests.test_stripped_item_miss_at_add_is_still_: the other side: a request whose item came without data that the engine no longer holds gets the retryable miss, and with its data it is added (round 2's behaviour kept).
tests.test_text_scheduling_on_prefix_cache_rer: a text workload through the engine's handler and the real AsyncScheduler with prefix caching, chunked prefill and a stand-in runner (sink-rejection contract): a 100-token prompt, its re-run with the same salt, with a fresh salt, three short prompts with a re-run arriving among them, a 300-token prompt prefilled in 64-token chunks, its re-run, a 340-token prompt extending it, three more short prompts. Pins each request's computed tokens and blocks at admission (prefix hits 96, 96, 288, 288; 0 elsewhere) and the sha256 of all 73 steps (scheduled tokens, computed tokens, block counts, finishes), both recorded on candidate-54.
tests.test_requests_without_multimodal_attribu: request stand-ins without mm_features (as test_stall_diagnostics.py and test_admission_control.py build them) go through EngineCoreProc._handle_client_request and AsyncLLM._add_request (fast path on) to candidate-54's add and send.

results.round 2 (plus the test file): 2 failed, 2 passed: test_text_request_enters_the_engine_as_before (DID NOT RAISE: round 2's handler turns the error into a multimodal miss for a request without items) and test_requests_without_multimodal_attributes_take_the_earlier_paths (AttributeError: request.mm_features read on a stand-in); the scheduling pin and the stripped-item test pass

new_test.what_failing_on_round_2_means: The two tests that fail on round 2's tree fail on structural differences: the handler's wrapper around every request, and reading mm_features on every request. Neither is reached by a real text request (add_request raises MultiModalCacheMissError only from the stripped-item check, which needs items; a real EngineCoreRequest always has mm_features). The scheduling pin cannot fail on round 2's tree, because round 2's text scheduling is candidate-54's: the replay shows it on the gate's own requests. So no test failing on round 2 identifies a cause of the gate's difference, and none can; the test that pins scheduling passes on both rounds.
